h: Airships, airfields and a coastline to match
p: Here's a fact to impress the family on the drive in: in July 1919 the airship R34 took off from East Fortune and made the first east-to-west crossing of the Atlantic by air, landing in New York. That gives you an idea of how deep this airfield's history runs, long before Concorde ever turned up.

Allow at least half a day. The site is spread out, the hangars are big, and the walk between them adds up, so comfy shoes are a must. Pack a coat for the open airfield too, because East Lothian breezes are no joke. It's best reached by car, as it sits out in farmland rather than in a town.

Once you've had your fill of planes, the East Lothian coast is right on your doorstep. North Berwick is a short drive away, with lovely beaches, a busy little high street and the Scottish Seabird Centre looking out towards the Bass Rock, home to an enormous gannet colony. Nearby, Tantallon Castle perches dramatically on the clifftops, and Dirleton Castle has some of the oldest gardens around.

Head inland instead and the market town of Haddington makes a pleasant stop for lunch, while East Linton is a pretty village with a river walk. Put it all together and you've got a proper day out: jets in the morning, castles or beaches in the afternoon and a bag of chips on the way home.
